lines.trans: Well, let's try your famous signature sauce.
This sauce is true high culinary art.
Oh, the fresh bread fell on the floor.
Right now we will quickly bring you new bread.
No, I am in a big hurry for an important meeting.
But you must taste this rare masterpiece!
I will return at exactly seven o'clock tonight.
We will prepare the very best sauce for you.
Agreed, Viktor, do not let me down tonight.
The Chef never deceives his favorite guests.
Until tonight then, I wish you great work.
We await you in the kitchen with great joy.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
Secondary conversational sense ('party, evening event') (e.g. a school evening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'meeting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('see you') (in 'до встречи' = until we meet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'high', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: 'договоримся' = we'll work something out

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: + dative of person + genitive of thing: желаю вам удачи

examples.trans: Good health to you, sir! (I wish you health!)

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('famous, celebrated').

examples.text: Ты ещё не понял? Ты теперь знаменитый!
examples.trans: Haven't you understood yet? You're famous now!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'art', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Read The Art of War, by Sun Tzu!
She loves modern art very much.
This is a real culinary work of art!

meanings.note: connected with cooking or the kitchen

examples.text: Я отличный повар и закончил кулинарный колледж.
examples.trans: I am an excellent cook and finished culinary college.

examples.text: Ладно, сейчас проверим твои настоящие кулинарные навыки.
examples.trans: Fine, now we will test your real culinary skills.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Secondary conversational sense ('beloved, darling') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Я никогда в жизни не пробовал такой вкусной утки!
examples.trans: I have never in my life tasted such delicious duck!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.en: come on, go on, let's see
meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('come on') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go on, tell me: how much is here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'манывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to deceive, to cheat', paired with 'обмануть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to lie to') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Потому что она простая. Её все обманывают.
examples.trans: Because she's naive. Everybody cheats her.

meanings.note: usually in short form обязан/обязана + dative + instrumental

examples.trans: You are obliged to come on time.

examples.text: Ты выпустишь меня под подписку о невыезде. И ты мне больше ничем не обязан.
examples.trans: You'll release me on a travel ban. And you won't owe me anything anymore.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('oh') used directly in spoken exchanges.

Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'вести'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to let down', forming an aspectual pair with 'подводить'.

examples.trans: I will never let you down.

examples.text: Надёжный друг никогда не подведёт в беде.
examples.trans: A reliable friend will never let you down in trouble.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.
examples.trans: Let us sum up your first work week.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'floor', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to try, to attempt') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'joy'.

examples.text: Он бы сейчас до потолка прыгал от радости.
examples.trans: He would be jumping to the ceiling for joy right now.
What a joy to see you!

examples.text: Мы с радостью сообщаем вам новость. Ваш долг полностью аннулирован!
examples.trans: We gladly inform you of the news. Your debt is completely canceled!

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to taste properly', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.

examples.text: Шеф ещё не распробовал новое блюдо.
examples.trans: The chef hasn't properly tasted the new dish yet.

examples.text: Подожди, я сам ещё не распробовал.
examples.trans: Wait, I haven't properly tasted it myself yet.

examples.text: Но вы обязаны распробовать этот редкий шедевр!
examples.trans: But you must taste this rare masterpiece!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'rare', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: У меня есть много редких материалов.
Макс, почему редкие трюфели оказались на помойке?
examples.trans: Max, why did rare truffles end up in the dumpster?

examples.text: Но вы обязаны распробовать этот редкий шедевр!
examples.trans: But you must taste this rare masterpiece!

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Secondary conversational sense ('evenly, smoothly') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'fresh', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('seven') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.text: Там депозит на семь тысяч рублей!
examples.trans: There's a deposit for seven thousand roubles!

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

спешить.gloss: to hurry, be in a rush

meanings.en: to hurry, rush, be in a hurry
meanings.note: куда ты спешишь? = where are you rushing to?

examples.trans: What happened? Where are you rushing to?
We are in a big hurry for the train.
Wait a bit, Sokolov. Do not hurry.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'пасть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fall', forming an aspectual pair with 'падать'.

examples.trans: The cup fell off the table.

examples.text: А потом на меня упал мусор с ветки.
examples.trans: And then rubbish fell on me from a branch.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'signature' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Я могу приготовить своё фирменное блюдо.
examples.trans: I can prepare my signature dish.
The chef prepared his signature dish.

meanings.note: plural хлеба, stressed on the ending
plural хлеба, stressed on the ending

examples.trans: The bread is on the table.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hour', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('o'clock') (в два часа = at two o'clock) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

час.governs: after 2, 3, 4 and полтора the genitive часа is stressed on the ending

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'masterpiece', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A masterpiece was made out of nothing.
This soup is a real masterpiece.
Well done. Practically a masterpiece out of nothing.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
